record.category: Usenet provider with web-to-Usenet interface (United States) - no free trial

free_tier.stated: None. The vendor's own help centre says: "Easynews does not offer a traditional free trial. Instead, it provides a 30-day money back guarantee on all new plans." The plans page sells "30-Day Money-Back Guarantee" as the risk-free route.
free_tier.notes: Affiliate pages advertise "14 days or 10 GB of data from Easynews"; the vendor's own knowledge base denies a free trial. The vendor page is the evidence and the affiliate claim is false.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap is published. The unit of retrieval is a Usenet article, roughly 750 KB by convention.

retention.stated: "6432+ Days Article Retention" on the Big Gig row; a checkout page read the same day said "6643+ Days". The conservative figure is kept.
retention.notes: Two vendor surfaces give different day counts on the same day; the smaller is recorded.

egress.terms: Metered by monthly data allowance on the Big Gig plan (150 GB/month); the unlimited-data plan is priced separately. No per-TB overage price is published on the page read.

record.interface_detail: Web-to-Usenet browser interface plus NNTP (200+ days on the mail-in Classic, 6432+ days on Big Gig, 60 connections). The web interface is the distinguishing feature; the schema has no nntp token, so the second token is unknown.
record.tooling: browser (no client needed); NNTP clients also work
record.chaining: Not a free step. It is the fallback when a Usenet indexer returns an article wanted in a browser: pay $9.99 for month one and use the 30-day refund as the trial, which still means a card.

limits.value: 150 GB/month on Big Gig; unlimited on the unlimited plan

record.binding_note: 150 GB/month on the entry plan is 15% of 1 TiB of monthly transfer; the unlimited plan removes the counter but requires the $9.99 monthly relationship. A card is required either way.

identity_cost.detail: Every plan is a paid subscription; the 30-day guarantee is a refund against a charge, not a free tier. The checkout asks for an email address and one of three payment methods: a credit card (first name, last name, zip code, country and card number), PayPal, or cryptocurrency (BTC and other coins); a cryptocurrency purchase is not refundable. The form has no phone field.

record.reliability_note: The refund requires a request inside 30 days; the vendor KB documents the policy. No suspension report was read.
record.confidence_note: Both the absence of a trial and the plan numbers are quoted from vendor pages read. The vendor's own KB contradicts the affiliate claim of a 10 GB trial.

evidence.proved: "Easynews does not offer a traditional free trial. Instead, it provides a 30-day money back guarantee on all new plans."
"30-Day Money-Back Guarantee", "Big Gig Plan" at "$29.94 / $9.99 /mo First 3 Months", "150 GB/Month Data", "6432+ Days Article Retention", "60 Connections"
"6643 days of article retention" in the body - the higher of two vendor figures for the same day
'Easynews accepts Visa, Mastercard, Discover, and American Express' and 'PayPal: Subscriptions can be managed through PayPal', plus the region caveat
the unlimited-plan checkout asks for an email address and offers three payment methods, Credit Card, PayPal and Cryptocurrency; a cryptocurrency purchase is not refundable
evidence.quote: Purchases with cryptocurrency are not eligible for refund.

evidence.proved: the checkout form's account field is an email address; the card option asks for first name, last name, zip code, country and card number, and the form has no phone field

record.notes: Repeatability: not applicable, because there is no free trial to repeat. Abandonment: if a free trial appears in the help centre, this becomes a trial record. PayPal is listed, but PayPal guest checkout still requires a funding card, and Easynews presents PayPal as a subscription authorisation rather than a one-off, so it is not a cardless route.

extras.affiliate_claim_refuted: "Click here for 14 days or 10 GB of data from Easynews" (shareconnector.net) against the vendor KB's "does not offer a traditional free trial"
